The ADaM metadata to give an AI assistant

Source: R/ai_metadata.R
tfl_adam_metadata.Rd

One data frame, one row a variable, of what an assistant may name when it writes specs: the datasets, their variables, labels and kinds, and each variable's levels (its code list's values). It is what tflspec_ai_manual() writes as 08_adam_metadata.csv, what tfl_ai_context() takes as datasets, and what tfl_ai_review() checks a spec's names against.

Usage

tfl_adam_metadata(
  define = NULL,
  adam_spec = NULL,
  datasets = NULL,
  max_levels = 30L
)

Arguments

define

A define.xml, or a tfl_read_define() result.

adam_spec

An ADaM spec workbook (.xlsx, read by tfl_read_define_spec() with its default profile), or a tfl_read_define_spec() result.

datasets

The ADaM datasets: a named list of data frames (list(ADSL = adsl, ADAE = adae)), or a metadata frame of this form already.

max_levels

For datasets: the most distinct values a character column may have for them to be listed as its levels.

Value

A data frame: dataset, dataset_label, variable, label, kind (character, numeric, date, factor, logical), levels (the values, " | " between them; NA for none), codelist (the code list's name or OID; NA for none) and source ("define.xml", "ADaM spec" or "datasets"), with attr(, "source").

Details

Give one source. When several are given, the first of this order is used, and a message says which:

  1. define: the study's define.xml (tfl_read_define()), the delivered datasets as described for submission;

  2. adam_spec: the ADaM specification workbook (tfl_read_define_spec()), for when the define is older than the data or not written yet;

  3. datasets: the datasets themselves, of which only the column information is taken: the names, the labels (the label attribute), the kinds, the levels of a factor, and the distinct values of a short coded character column (at most max_levels of them). A subject's values never are: identifiers (...ID), dates and times (...DTC, ...DT, ...DTM, ...TM) and free text (a value longer than 40 characters) are left without levels.

Two sources that disagree (a variable renamed in the spec but not yet in the define) would leave the assistant to choose, which is why one is used.

See also

tflspec_ai_manual() for the kit it goes into.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("xml2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  md <- tfl_adam_metadata(define = system.file("extdata", "define",
                                               "define.xml",
                                               package = "tflspec"))
  md[md$variable %in% c("SEX", "AGEGR1"), c("dataset", "variable", "levels")]
}
#>    dataset variable     levels
#> 3     ADSL   AGEGR1 <65 | >=65
#> 4     ADSL      SEX      M | F
#> 10    ADAE      SEX      M | F
# from the data: names, labels, kinds and short code lists only
adsl <- data.frame(USUBJID = c("01-001", "01-002"), SEX = c("F", "M"),
                   AGE = c(63, 71))
tfl_adam_metadata(datasets = list(ADSL = adsl))
#>   dataset dataset_label variable label      kind levels codelist   source
#> 1    ADSL          <NA>  USUBJID  <NA> character   <NA>     <NA> datasets
#> 2    ADSL          <NA>      SEX  <NA> character  F | M     <NA> datasets
#> 3    ADSL          <NA>      AGE  <NA>   numeric   <NA>     <NA> datasets
